_comment: MSV3 fleet registry. Binds each probe's sensor ID to the BLE addresses it is allowed to
appear on and to the bootloader currently installed on it.
Why this file exists: SENSOR_ID is a hand-edited constant in MSV3_Moisture_BLE_Sleep.ino, and
scripts/ble_ota_update.py targets a raw BLE address. Nothing previously connected the two, so
an image built for one probe could be sent to another -- giving two probes the same sensor ID
and silently mixing two plants' data in the receiver. The flasher now resolves --probe N
through this file and refuses any address or package identity that disagrees with it.
application_address is the address the running application advertises on. recovery_address is
application_address + 1, which is where the bootloader advertises when it starts with NO valid
application. After a successful buttonless jump the bootloader instead reuses
application_address, because the peer-data handoff carries it across the reset -- so BOTH
addresses are legitimate bootloader locations and the flasher accepts either.
device_type is the two-byte DFU target tag the installed bootloader accepts: 0x0052 is
Adafruit's stock constant, 0x3356 is what MSV3's own bootloader build replaces it with. It
stops stock-packaged images installing; it is NOT a security property and NOT model-specific.
legacy_package_sha256 allowlists specific pre-65538 application images for one probe. Below
that version the advertised name is not provably equal to the compiled SENSOR_ID, so on a
deployed probe --allow-legacy-package alone is refused; only an image hashed here gets
through. Add one only when deployment records establish that exact image. Empty is correct
when you have no such record -- rebuild instead.
bootloader_key_sha256 pins the SHA-256 of the 64-byte P-256 public point (Qx||Qy) that the
probe's installed bootloader was built to trust. ble_ota_update.py checks the release
manifest's key against it before verifying a signature, so changing the client's trust root
takes a visible edit here as well as to the manifest. 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 share one trust root.
deployed=true means the probe is expected to be advertising, so msv3_fleet_scan.py treats
its absence as a problem. The bench board is deployed=false: it sits powered off most of the
time and its silence says nothing.
'observed' fields record a real scan or transfer, 'inferred' fields have not been seen yet.

installed_application_version is bookkeeping: the bootloader cannot report what it is running. Stock and MSV3 1.0.1 do not enforce it; MSV3 1.0.2+ also records and enforces an on-device anti-rollback floor. ble_ota_update.py independently refuses a package below this value unless --allow-downgrade. Update it after every successful transfer. 0 disables the host-side check.

swd_accessible is MUTABLE PHYSICAL STATE, not history: are this probe's SWD/USB pads reachable RIGHT NOW? Conformal coating makes it false. SET IT FALSE THE MOMENT A PROBE IS COATED -- arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 refuses to build a deliberately-hanging -HangTest image for any probe where this is false, and that refusal is the only thing standing between a coated probe and an image that never opens a radio window.

guard2_validated is a DURABLE FACT and deliberately separate: this hardware has actually demonstrated the watchdog-loop -> BLE DFU escape. Having passed the test once does not make a coated probe recoverable today, so nothing gates on this field; it records what has been proven so a future session does not have to guess.

probes.name: MSV3-MOISTURE-004
probes.notes: The water-immersion board. Migrated off the stock bootloader 2026-09-03 and updated over BLE alone. In soil, battery + solar. Running build 2026-09-05-guard1 (guard 1 only; ENABLE_BOOT_FAILURE_GUARD is staged off until the watchdog-hang test runs with SWD). Confirmed 2026-09-05 00:55 PDT: -72 dBm, 3983 mV, flags 0x1c, DIS reports the build over BLE, receiver ingesting with no false faults. PROVENANCE GAP, recorded 2026-09-05: the exact package installed on this probe was never archived -- it was built into the gitignored .arduino-build/ path, which later builds overwrote, and its source carried an uncommitted SENSOR_ID edit that no commit describes. The running image therefore cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte from this repository. Since 2026-09-05 identity is a build parameter (arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 -SensorId), so (commit, sensor id, build tag) reproduces an image exactly and this cannot recur. Rebuild an equivalent with -SensorId 4 before the next OTA to this probe, and archive the package. This is the battery-powered production unit; final provisioning and coating remain deferred until probes 6 and 7 have exercised the conformal-coating process and functional Probe 6 passes its post-cure check. SOLAR AND CHARGING STATE, measured 2026-09-19: probe 4 sits in the shared Alocasia pot WITH its solar panel. Eight consecutive days 2026-09-06..09-13 show a clean 11:00-16:00 charging ramp of +25 to +90 mV, peaking at 4310 mV, which is the as-built ~4.26 V ceiling. The probe then went off the air on 2026-09-14 -- the R11/R14 rework date -- and returned on 2026-09-18 at 4034 mV. On 2026-09-19 the ramp is GONE: -6 mV across those same hours on the HIGHEST insolation of the entire series (die-temp excursion 8.62 C, against 5.25-7.00 C on the charging days), with wake cadence unchanged at 70 s/wake and the cell falling -53.6 mV/day (r2=0.982). This board RECEIVED the 2026-09-14 rework to 3.887 V nominal VBAT_OV: MSV3_VBAT_OV_STORAGE_REWORK_2026-09-14.md carries a per-board table stating that all field probes EXCEPT MSV3-MOISTURE-007 were swapped on 2026-09-14 (maintainer). That document lives on main (commit edc9705) and NOT on this branch, which is why an earlier version of this note called the rework a hypothesis. It establishes the documented record, not an independent check of the fitted resistors. NOT YET PROVEN: a dead harvester produces identical telemetry. THRESHOLD SEMANTICS -- do not quote a single number. VBAT_OV nominal 3.887 V; on this board ~3.897 V using its own backed-out VBIAS 1.2532 V; ceiling corner band with 1% resistors 3.857-3.937 V; restart is VBAT_OV minus VBAT_OV_HYST whose range is 18/35/89 mV, so the RESTART band is ~3.768-3.919 V, about 151 mV wide. At -53.6 mV/day from 3988 mV the test window is roughly 2026-09-20 to 09-24. Judge it on whether the daytime ramp RETURNS, not on any voltage. WHY IT CURRENTLY READS ABOVE ITS OWN CEILING: the rework did not touch the BQ25170 USB path (R8 = 27k, 4.20 V), and this probe was on USB while off-air 2026-09-14..09-18, so it was charged above the harvester ceiling by a different path and is descending through the dead band. PHYSICAL CHECK from the rework doc: power from the panel with a cell attached and watch VSTOR -- it should plateau near 3.90 V and ripple to ~3.86 V before charging resumes; a probe still stopping near 4.26 V has the resistors reversed or unswapped.

The 16:38 split point recorded in earlier notes is WRONG: it pulls the deleted block D and the entire bench block E into the series and produces nonsense slopes (+9.0 %/C, r2=0.21). || 2026-09-18 16:55 SUPERSEDED BY v65567 (MSV3-BUILD:2026-09-18-hybridv12-airpad, -HybridV12Tank -HybridMuxCode 0), installed over BLE in 41 s; archived msv3-1.0.1-sensor004-v65567-signed-ota.zip. Measures on mux code 0 only (also the sleep code, so the mux never moves): tank = L + board + MSV3 electrode as padding + the v1.2 sensor (sense trace to TANK_HOT, its ground U to TANK_COLD, jumpers, no solder). The MSV3 electrode MUST be held in AIR for this to be valid: the 2026-09-15 glass-of-water test read it flat in air for a full day. DIS read back hybridv12-airpad; 200 s scan wake +1, flags 0x54, 4028 mV, die 24.00 C, DATA_CH0 38,277,081 (~6.2 MHz, ~98 pF, in range). || EARLIER SAME DAY: INVERTED HYBRID TEST. The maintainer wired an external v1.2 capacitive sensor to the C17 pads (C17 already removed), so it sits directly across the FDC tank. Signed v65566 (MSV3-BUILD:2026-09-18-hybridv12, -HybridV12Tank, IDRIVE 16, Guard 2 off) installed over BLE in 37 s through the resident 1.0.1 bootloader; archived as MSV3/bootloader/generated/1.0.1/msv3-1.0.1-sensor004-v65566-signed-ota.zip. Before the jump DIS reported the previous build as 2026-09-10-p4-settle1024, NOT 2026-09-05-guard1 as the notes above say. Post-install: DIS read back 2026-09-18-hybridv12; a 200 s scan saw wake +2, flags 0x54 (capless bit 6 set, phase 0 only, bareValid clear), 4028 mV, die 25.25 C, DATA_CH0 65,234,409, OTA gate open. The image measures ONLY on mux code 2 (electrodes disconnected; tank = L + TMUX off-capacitance + v1.2 sensor) and parks on code 0 in sleep. 65.2M counts is about 10.5 MHz, ABOVE the FDC2214's 10 MHz sensor ceiling and the 8.75 MHz FIN_SEL=01 range, so readings are out of datasheet range until fixed capacitance is added across the tank; the image rejects the 0x0FFFFFFF over-range sentinel. To return to production afterwards, build a new capless production image above 65567; the archived capless v65564 is below it and ble_ota_update.py will refuse it (bootloader 1.0.1 has no on-device floor, but --allow-downgrade is not for ordinary updates).

probes.name: MSV3-MOISTURE-005
probes.notes: Bootloader 1.0.3 installed over SWD on 2026-09-08. Signed application v65555 (MSV3-BUILD:2026-09-08-prod5; Guard 1 and Guard 2 on; serial logs off) installed over BLE from recovery address F9:18:9B:CA:10:B3 in 28 s. DIS read back the exact build ID. A 150-second scan observed 29 packets across two advancing wakes (+1), valid sensor data, 4411 mV, flags 0x1c, and an open OTA gate. The 4411 mV observation was while USB-powered with no battery attached, so it is not a cell-voltage measurement. Equality-version rescue package SHA-256: 0198dd469cbc2ba411b73f310c5d0054e84abe9a5bd7c0dc1db60faf46ddf735. || 2026-09-19 CAPLESS TRANSITION AND REDEPLOYMENT INTO THE SHARED ALOCASIA POT. The maintainer placed this probe in the shared pot as the MSV3-blade + FDC arm of the electrode/readout comparison (it was mistaken for probe 8 at the time; probe 8 remains deployed=false and unseen). It came back on the air after six days dark (last prior row 2026-09-14 03:05 UTC) still running pre-capless v65555, and its first rows were UNUSABLE: moisture computed to 0 on moisture_scale 2, with bare_tank_fdc_counts 65,456,050-65,562,392 -- above the FDC2214 10 MHz ceiling, the same out-of-range failure as probe 4's deleted v65566 block, because a pre-capless image still measures a bare-tank reference that C17-removed hardware no longer has. C17 REMOVAL IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT on this board: raw_fdc_counts moved from ~19.85M on 2026-09-14 (C17-installed regime) to ~36.2M now (C17-removed regime), matching probe 8's ~20.49M / ~39.41M split. FIX: signed capless v65564 (MSV3-BUILD:2026-09-14-capless-prod5) installed over BLE in 32 s through the resident 1.0.3 bootloader; the package had been built 2026-09-14 alongside probe 6's and never installed. Preflight passed integrity, boot-guard and identity. DIS PROVEN by a deliberate same-package re-run, which the already-running-build guard REFUSED before any jump, reading back 2026-09-14-capless-prod5 -- the probe was never taken off the air to prove it. A 200 s scan then saw 34 packets at -71 dBm, wake advancing +1, 4310 mV (USB, NOT a cell measurement), flags 0x54 (capless bit 6 SET, bareValid CLEAR), die 21.75 C, DATA_CH0 35,490,875, OTA gate open. Cloud rows confirm the switch in place: moisture_scale 2 -> 3, bare_tank_fdc_counts 65.5M -> NULL, moisture 0 -> ~44,500. PHASE GAP RESOLVED: a scan taken WHILE the probe was being inserted reported phase 1 at 152,328,492 against phase 0 at 36,335,033, a 115,993,458 gap that tripped the analog-path warning. After settling the gap is 47,934, far under the 1,200,000 threshold. That alarm was insertion transients, NOT a probe-7-style cracked TMUX joint -- do not scan this board while handling it. OPEN CAUTION: it is running on USB in the same pot whose AM rig (sensor 3) showed cyclic mains-coupling noise bands traced to the receiver PSU sharing an outlet. The thermal signal being measured here is a sub-1% daily wobble, so move it to battery, or at least a different outlet from the receiver, before its data is used for the electrode-versus-readout comparison.

probes.notes: DEPLOYED 2026-09-16 in a pot as the SP+ shunt-zener overcharge-clamp trial (maintainer). Clamp part is a TEMPORARY 1N4728A (3.3 V, soft knee), which held SP+ below 2.2 V in direct sun; a better part is on order, so readings before and after the swap are not directly comparable. Uncoated. Running signed capless production v65565 (MSV3-BUILD:2026-09-14-capless-prod7-restore; Guard 2 on), package SHA-256 2ed999de3cb189f2f353fb562de615b2b9db5afc29e766ee086d423f69f5b456. The on-device rollback floor is 65565; do not use the older v65556 rescue. BQ25504 OV DIVIDER IS AS-BUILT: the 2026-09-14 R11/R14 storage rework was not done on this board before its battery and panel were fitted (maintainer, 2026-09-16), so R11=5.62M / R14=4.42M programs VBAT_OV to about 4.26 V, not 3.89 V. Judge the clamp trial against that ceiling: probe 4 capped cleanly at 4309 mV telemetry WHILE IT WAS STILL ON THE AS-BUILT DIVIDER, while the unclamped body-diode path drove probe 6 to about 4.44-4.49 V. CORRECTION 2026-09-19: probe 4 is NO LONGER a live same-divider peer. That 4309 mV observation is from 2026-09-13, the day before the R11/R14 rework, and probe 6's diagnostic_state records that the rework went to every field probe except probe 7. Probe 4's own telemetry corroborates it: its solar charging ramp disappeared after it returned on 2026-09-18, at a cell voltage 270 mV BELOW the as-built ceiling. Probe 7 is therefore the only board known to be on the as-built divider and its 4.26 V ceiling has no contemporaneous comparison. CHARGING, measured 2026-09-19: probe 7 went 4002 -> 4121 mV across 2026-09-16..09-19, +40.6 mV/day net, with daytime slopes of +7.9, +15.8 and +6.4 mV/h. The 2026-09-16 reassessment's estimate of 0.7-1.2 mAh/day net (a nearly flat battery) is NOT supported by the data -- the temporary 1N4728A is not halving the harvest to zero. Projected to reach the ceiling ~2026-09-23, which is the real clamp test: capping near 4309 mV means the clamp works; continuing toward 4.44-4.49 V means it does not. swd_accessible is false because the board is potted, not coated; pull it from the pot to reach SWD.

_comment: CONFOUND, recorded 2026-09-19. Three of the four electrode x readout corners in the shared
Alocasia pot share ONE mains outlet. The fourth, probe 4, is battery-only and galvanically
isolated -- and it is also the quietest rig by 4-5x. Power topology is therefore confounded
with the factorial, and any AM-vs-FDC conclusion inherits it.
Sensor 3 already has a documented history of cyclic noise bands traced to the receiver PSU
sharing an outlet with the bench rig, so this is a measured failure mode on this exact setup,
not a theoretical one.

shared_outlet.detail: sensor 3 = ESP32-powered v1.2 rig; sensor 9 = ESP32-powered hybrid rig; probe 5 = USB from the computer. All on the same outlet.

isolated.detail: probe 4 = battery only plus solar; sensor 2 = battery.

consequences: DEMOTED 2026-09-19 (maintainer observation): sensors 3 and 9 are BOTH ESP32-powered on the SAME outlet, yet s3 is ~2.9x more thermally immune than s9 (per-day: s3 8.04/9.86/7.54 mV/C vs s9 20.35/21.41/31.20 mV/C against probe 6's room reference). Identical mains exposure, 3x different thermal response -- so mains coupling does NOT explain which rigs are thermally quiet here.

Therefore 'probe 4 is quiet because it is battery-isolated' is a WEAK alternative, not a co-equal explanation. The v1.2 electrode is quiet hardwired (s3) and quiet on battery (probe 4); the blade is noisy hardwired (s9).
STILL CLEAN and now doing double duty: the within-AM comparison (s3 vs s9) is both the load-bearing electrode result and the control that demotes this confound.
STILL WORTH REMOVING: the topology asymmetry is real even if it is not the explanation. Moving probe 5 to battery makes the FDC row power-matched.

OPEN PREDICTION: if the electrode is the variable, probe 5 (blade + FDC, on USB) should be NOISY like sensor 9 despite sharing probe 4's readout. If probe 5 is quiet like probe 4, the readout is the variable instead. Cheapest remaining discriminator; needs only clean days.

_comment: The maintainer's physical reading of what drives noise and thermal drift, stated 2026-09-19.
READ THIS BEFORE ANALYSING THERMAL DATA. It is a TWO-FACTOR model: the readout and the electrode
each contribute their own noise term and their own temperature term, and they are separable.
Sessions have repeatedly tried to force a single-factor answer ('is it the electrode OR the
readout') and got stuck. The answer is BOTH, which is why the apparent electrode effect changes
size depending on which readout it is measured through.
explains: Why the apparent electrode effect changed size with the readout it was measured through (1.36x within the AM pair, ~4x within the FDC pair): the readout adds its own temperature term on top.
Why sensor 3 (v1.2 electrode + v1.2 driving circuit) shows LARGE drift but a LOW thermal coefficient -- noisy circuit, immune electrode.
Why sensor 9 (MSV3 blade + v1.2 driving circuit) shows CLEAN traces with a HIGH thermal coefficient -- low-temp circuit, very-susceptible electrode.
Why probe 4 (v1.2 electrode + FDC) is the flattest rig measured -- low-noise readout AND immune electrode, the best available pairing.
Why probe 4 BEFORE 2026-09-18, when it was MSV3 blade + FDC, was strongly thermal (-0.387 %/C, 2.60% daily swing), and probe 8 on the same pairing wobbled 1.956%.
prediction_probe5: Probe 5 is MSV3 blade + FDC, the pairing that stacks the VERY-susceptible electrode with the susceptible readout.
PREDICTION: probe 5 should show the LARGEST thermal response of the four corners, and because the FDC readout is low-noise it should show it CLEANLY -- the most legible thermal signature in the pot.
This is falsifiable and needs no new hardware, only clean days on a probe already in the shared pot.

CAVEAT on sign: historically blade+FDC (probe 8) read DRIER when warm while v1.2+FDC (probe 4 now) reads WETTER when warm, so the electrode flips the sign within one readout. Do not assume the two temperature terms simply add; check the sign before fitting a combined magnitude.
